en: Now that we learned about single path
segments,
we can also work on the update and delete
function. And let's continue with deleting
because that's a bit easier.
As I mentioned, typically you use a POST
request for deleting unless you're building
a REST API, which we aren't doing here.
So therefore, I'll register a new POST
route.
And now again, the question is, what should
be the path here?
And I would say for deleting something, we
also need the ID of what should be deleted.
So even though that's a POST request, we
don't even need to transport any data in the
request body.
It just is a convention to use POST for
deleting because we manipulate something on
the server.
But we won't even need the POST request body
because we can again just encode the ID in
the URL
as we did it for getting a single element.
So we can grab that code and do the same
thing here for our delete post route.
Now these 2 routes here,
this GET route and the POST route, will be
different even though they have the same
path because they act on different HTTP
methods.
You couldn't have the same method and the
same path, that would not work. You must
only have one route per path method
combination. But here we got the same path
but different methods, and therefore these
technically are different routes that will
be executed for different kinds of incoming
requests.
And then here we have our good old
middleware
